Fig. 6 shows the stress-strain curves of the four multi-elemental Nb-Si based alloys compressed at 1250 °C with a strain rate of 0.005 s−1 and a height reduction of 30%.

After single addition of Mo or Zr, the compressive strength of 5Mo-0Zr or 0Mo-4Zr alloy increases to 361 or 273 MPa, respectively, indicating that the alloying element Mo or Zr can improves the compressive strength at 1250 °C of multi-elemental Nb-Si based alloys.

In 0Mo-4Zr alloy, the primary silicide blocks have also rotated to the direction perpendicular to the compression axis after compression, and some cracks are simultaneously observed in them, as shown in Fig. 7e.

As the 5Mo-4Zr alloy shows the highest strength peak (393 MPa) in the four alloys, it is suggested that the composite additions of Mo and Zr can further improve the compressive strength at 1250 °C of the alloys.

while the other three alloys only possess γ(Nb,X)5Si3, suggesting that both single and composite additions of Mo and Zr suppress the formation of α(Nb,X)5Si3 phase whilst promote the formation of γ(Nb,X)5Si3 phase.
